newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan deal to bolster B.C. treasury-report.
newsitem.headline: Alcan deal to bolster B.C. treasury-report.

text.p: British Columbia's settlement with Alcan Aluminium Ltd will mean a net gain to the province's treasury of C$20 million to C$100 million excluding benefits to the economy in general and removal of the risk of legal damages, according to an analysis released Thursday.

Alcan and the province announced Tuesday a deal that halted a lawsuit in which Alcan sought to recover damages for the province's cancellation of its half-built Kemano hydroelectric project. As part of the settlement, Alcan committed to try to build a new C$1.2 billion aluminum smelter at its Kitimat works in northern British Columbia.
The province released Thursday a financial analysis of the agreement by RBC Dominion Securities that concluded the deal was a "reasonable and prudent course of action."
The analysis noted that the province avoided legal action. Alcan had sought the recoup the C$535 million already spent on Kemano plus interest and other costs.

Moreover, the firm said that between now and the projected end-of-life for the new smelter the deal "would appear to result in a net impact upon the province's fiscal position in the range of C$20-C$100 million net present value, before including the benefits of litigation avoided."
In addition it said independent estimates that the smelter would boost provincial gross domestic product by C$970 million during construction and C$285 million from operations were reasonable.
